♻ ☆ Decoupled Data Consistency with Diffusion Purification for Image Restoration
Xiang Li, Soo Min Kwon, Shijun Liang, Ismail R. Alkhouri, Saiprasad Ravishankar, Qing Qu
Diffusion models have recently gained traction as a powerful class of deep generative priors, excelling in a wide range of image restoration tasks due to their exceptional ability to model data distributions. To solve image restoration problems, many existing techniques achieve data consistency by incorporating additional likelihood gradient steps into the reverse sampling process of diffusion models. However, the additional gradient steps pose a challenge for real-world practical applications as they incur a large computational overhead, thereby increasing inference time. They also present additional difficulties when using accelerated diffusion model samplers, as the number of data consistency steps is limited by the number of reverse sampling steps. In this work, we propose a novel diffusion-based image restoration solver that addresses these issues by decoupling the reverse process from the data consistency steps. Our method involves alternating between a reconstruction phase to maintain data consistency and a refinement phase that enforces the prior via diffusion purification. Our approach demonstrates versatility, making it highly adaptable for efficient problem-solving in latent space. Additionally, it reduces the necessity for numerous sampling steps through the integration of consistency models. The efficacy of our approach is validated through comprehensive experiments across various image restoration tasks, including image denoising, deblurring, inpainting, and super-resolution.
♻ ☆ Implicit Neural Models for Direct Multi-Shell Diffusion MRI Signal Estimation
Sanna Persson, Fabian Leander Sinzinger, Christoffer Olsson, Rodrigo Moreno
Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging is a noninvasive technique that is sensitive to the motion of water molecules in human tissue. The image signal is commonly described in q-space; however, a complete coverage of this space is often infeasible due to hardware and acquisition time limitations. In this work, we propose to represent the entire diffusion signal using an implicit neural representation network with wavelet activation functions. The signal space is encoded using Fourier features and spherical harmonics basis functions for a continuous output distribution of the raw diffusion data, enabling both super-resolution and q-space interpolation. Additionally, we introduce a pretraining strategy using a group template, enabling faster per-subject optimisation when combined with nonlinear registrations of subjects into template space. We tested the method with 10 subjects from the Human Connectome Project and 26 subjects from in-house data (multidimensional diffusion MRI from a Parkinson's disease cohort). The results show that the proposed method yields high-fidelity reconstructions with significantly reduced memory requirements compared to raw diffusion-weighted images. The pretraining scheme showed good generalisability properties on data acquired with very different protocols. We further assess the method on downstream metrics relevant to diffusion MRI data from the learned representations.

♻ ☆ Disentangling and Fusing Neurostructural and Vascular Ageing for Retinal Age Prediction
Junwen Zheng, Li Rong Wang, Anthony Zihan Lin, Xinran Xu, Wei Kiong Ngo, Kelvin Zhenghao Li, Tock Han Lim, Xiuyi Fan
Estimating biological age is an important task in ageing research, as it quantifies individual ageing trajectories beyond chronological age. Retinal age estimation has become a well-established direction in this area because retinal imaging provides a non-invasive window into neural and microvascular ageing. Existing studies, however, have predominantly focused on fundus photographs and usually model retinal ageing as a single generic process. Although biological ageing is heterogeneous and different organs or tissues may age at different rates, little research has explicitly distinguished neurostructural and vascular ageing in retinal age prediction. This work fills this gap by studying neurostructural ageing with Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) images and vascular ageing with Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography (OCTA) images. We formulate multimodal OCT/OCTA retinal age estimation as a structural-vascular ageing decomposition problem and propose SAP-DPF, a unified dual-path prediction framework that separately estimates structural and vascular ageing, models modality-specific predictive uncertainty, and adaptively fuses the two ageing signals through an uncertainty-gated late-fusion module. Using this unified prediction framework, SAP-DPF achieves a mean absolute error of 4.07 years for the structural pathway and 7.37 years for the vascular pathway, while the proposed late-fusion algorithm further improves the overall mean absolute error to 4.02 years, representing a 12.52% improvement over the strongest single-modality baseline. This work could extend retinal age prediction beyond a single biological-age estimate, providing a framework for investigating structural and vascular contributions to heterogeneous retinal ageing.

♻ ☆ Diagnosing Diversity Collapse and Validating Mask-Conditioned Diffusion for Labeled Microtubule Microscopy
Mario Koddenbrock, Frederic Rapp, Simone Reber, Erik Rodner
Mask-conditioned diffusion models have become standard for generating labeled training data in biomedical imaging. But the tools used to evaluate them were built for a different problem. Standard metrics like FID and KID score images through ImageNet-trained features. Those features do not transfer to microscopy, leaving the metrics poorly calibrated for specialized domains. Even with a domain-appropriate feature space, a single blended number can still hide a real failure: a model can produce visually plausible images that still transfer poorly to downstream tasks. We identify a specific failure mode: Late in training, realism keeps improving while texture diversity collapses. The model settles onto a fixed color palette, converging to a high-similarity, low-diversity state that standard metrics do not penalize. Therefore, we propose a diversity-aware diagnostic in a domain-validated feature space. It combines a realism axis based on inter-similarity to real images with a diversity axis based on intra-similarity among generated samples. This diagnostic selects a checkpoint that domain experts cannot reliably distinguish from real recordings in a forced-choice study. It also yields useful downstream segmentation: a segmenter trained only on synthetically labeled data reaches a median skeletonised IoU comparable to one trained on real data, at lower cross-fold variance, and clearly ahead of the best available public alternative in this domain, a parametric renderer. We also reproduce a data-efficient hyperparameter-transfer experiment from prior work, tuning several foundation segmenters on a small labeled subset and evaluating on real images: transfer is stronger with our data. We release DiffuMT on HuggingFace, including the triplet dataset, code to reproduce the downstream-utility validation, and a standalone diagnostic tool for evaluating mask-conditioned diffusion models.

♻ ☆ Image CL-SEC: Cross-Layer Semantic Error Correction for Image Communication
Feifan Zhang, Xuelin Bai, Yirun Wang, Yuyang Du, Soung Chang Liew
Semantic error correction (SEC) uses the semantic knowledge of pretrained models to complement conventional channel decoding. By combining physical-layer decoding information with application-layer semantic predictions, cross-layer SEC (CL-SEC) has demonstrated substantial performance gains in text transmission; however, its applicability to image transmission remains largely unexplored. This paper proposes Image CL-SEC, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first extension of the CL-SEC framework to image transmission. Image CL-SEC uses channel-decoding information together with contextual predictions from a pretrained visual model to resolve residual uncertainty after forward error correction (FEC) decoding. In our implementation, images are represented as discrete visual tokens. For each token position selected for re-evaluation, the probability distribution produced by the channel decoder is combined with the distribution predicted by the visual model to identify the most likely transmitted token. The resulting decision therefore reflects both channel evidence and visual context. Experiments across multiple channel conditions show that, at low and moderate signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), Image CL-SEC improves pixel-level fidelity, perceptual similarity, and token-recovery accuracy relative to either channel decoding or visual-model inference alone. Supplementary experiments using different pretrained visual models further demonstrate that these gains are not specific to a single model.
♻ ☆ Harnessing Magnitude-Only and Complex Measurements for Improved Dynamic MRI Reconstruction with Learned Priors
Mahdi Saberi, Yaşar Utku Alçalar, Merve Gülle, Chetan Shenoy, Mehmet Akçakaya
MRI reconstruction methods for undersampled k-space data naturally utilize complex-valued measurements. Parallel developments in sparse phase retrieval have shown that magnitude-only measurements may provide complementary information for signal recovery. However, their use in MRI reconstruction remains largely unexplored, due to lack of practical settings where informative magnitude measurements can be obtained without additional scan time. In this work, we investigate the use of auxiliary k-space magnitude information for accelerated steady-state dynamic MRI reconstruction, and demonstrate strong consistency of k-space magnitudes across time-frames. Building on this observation, we propose $\mathbb{C}+\text{Mag}$, a magnitude-informed physics-driven deep learning reconstruction method. The proposed method employs an ADMM-based unrolling framework with a novel magnitude-aware data-fidelity formulation, where quadratically smoothed optimization and momentum-based updates are introduced to address the non-differentiability and non-convexity of the magnitude constraints. Experiments on retrospectively undersampled cine MRI and phase-contrast flow MRI datasets, as well as prospectively undersampled real-time cine MRI acquisitions, demonstrate improved artifact suppression, sharper anatomical recovery, and better preservation of phase information compared to conventional PD-DL methods, which is further supported through blinded expert reader evaluations.

☆ Deep Search in Real-World Web Environments
Xiaomin Yu, Hongliang Chen, Zhe Huang, Shilin Yan, Shao-Rong Su, Xuqiao Ma, Feiyang Wang, Jiayu Chen, Jiwei Fang, Yu Yan, Yini Huang, Chen Chen, Ruoxi Cheng, Yuzhi He, Yuhui Zhang, Xiaoxing Hu, Chen Liu, Jianbo Lin, Yijiang Li, Xiaobin Hu, Menglong Li, Zhuoran Lu, Weishi Wang, Zhongqi Yue, Chengwei Qin
Despite substantial progress in Deep Search agents, their ability to conduct end-to-end research in real-world open Web environments remains insufficiently evaluated. Unlike static retrieval settings, information on the real-world Web is distributed across diverse sources, modalities, and heterogeneous formats, often involving complex interaction mechanisms that require agents to autonomously search for, access, and integrate relevant evidence during execution. To address this gap, we introduce the OpenDS task, designed to evaluate agents' ability to perform multi-step deep search in the live, open Web. This task requires agents to autonomously explore the real Web, discover and connect relevant evidence from multiple independent sources through Web search, browser interaction, and evidence processing, and ultimately determine a unique factual answer. Building on this task formulation, we construct OpenDS-World, a benchmark comprising 200 challenging tasks spanning diverse information modalities, heterogeneous file formats, and interactive access requirements, with independent human verification to ensure evidence validity and answer uniqueness. We evaluate 12 frontier models under a unified tool environment and execution protocol. The best-performing model achieves 39.0% accuracy, while human evaluation across 1,000 independent attempts yields 21.1% accuracy. Further analyses of tool usage, search cost, termination behavior, and failure recovery reveal substantial differences in research strategies across models, as well as persistent challenges in tool coordination and long-horizon search management. OpenDS-World provides a unified evaluation platform for systematically assessing and advancing agents' autonomous deep search capabilities in real-world open Web environments.
☆ Omni-Woodpecker: Hallucination Correction via Evidence-Prior Rebalancing for Omni LLMs
Zijian Liu, Chaoyou Fu, Yan Yang, Caifeng Shan, Ran He
Recent Omni LLMs (OLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in joint audio-visual reasoning, yet cross-modal hallucinations remain a major challenge. Existing mitigation methods mainly operate at the output level, overlooking the entanglement of grounding evidence and learned priors within fused representations. To address this issue, we propose Omni-Woodpecker (OWP), a training-free framework that shifts hallucination mitigation from output-level manipulation to conflict-conditioned representation rebalancing. Specifically, OWP first identifies cross-modal conflicts from complementary modality-specific views. It then employs orthogonal decomposition to separate grounding evidence from competing priors within the hidden states. Finally, OWP adaptively rebalances fused representations by suppressing misleading priors and restoring ignored evidence before decoding. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and strong cross-architecture generalization of OWP. Using Qwen2.5-Omni-7B as the backbone, OWP improves performance by 12.9 and 8.6 points on CMM and AVHBench, respectively, while consistently achieving gains of 0.67-2.25 points across four general OLLM reasoning benchmarks. Furthermore, OWP generalizes effectively to VideoLLaMA2-AV, improving performance by 4.6 and 3.9 points on the same benchmarks. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/ZiiJianLiu/Omni-Woodpecker

☆ OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
Yu Zhou, Cheng-Fu Yang, Rui Sun, Di Wu, Sibo Peng, Mingyang Zhang, Zhen Yang, Ruiyi Zhang, Nanyun Peng, Zhe Gan, Kai-Wei Chang
Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made rapid progress on visual reasoning, yet many tasks require evidence that is difficult to obtain through internal reasoning alone: our controlled study on 22 benchmarks shows that simply increasing the inference budget of the base model yields only modest gains. Such tasks demand grounded perception, external knowledge, and numerical measurements obtained through heterogeneous tools, whose outputs must be made interpretable to the model and retained across reasoning steps. We introduce OpenVLHarness, a multimodal reasoning harness organized around a capability layer and persistent multimodal memory. The capability layer combines task-level tool interfaces with evidence rendering, providing consistent access to heterogeneous backends and converting their outputs into model-readable observations. Persistent multimodal memory retains the corresponding images, structured data, and web references as addressable artifacts throughout each query. A coding interface executes generated programs over stored data, enabling computations that combine results from multiple tools. Together, these mechanisms support an iterative process of acquiring, inspecting, and composing multimodal evidence. Evaluated on 22 benchmarks with eight open and proprietary backbones, OpenVLHarness improves average scores by 9.7-12.6 points over matched no-tool baselines, including +11.2 with Qwen3-VL-8B, +9.7 with Kimi K3, and +9.9 with GPT-6 Astra. With GPT-6 Luna at medium reasoning effort, OpenVLHarness outperforms the base model, Codex, and Visual Sketchpad at maximum effort by 7.7-8.5 points while incurring at most 37% of their model-token cost.
☆ Cassette-Editor: A Video Editing Agent That Edits the Way You Do
Zhixin Zeng, Jiahao Zhong
Language agents increasingly work by calling tools on a persistent artifact, such as a code repository, and the result of each call shapes their next step. Video editing is a demanding case of this pattern: what a frame shows depends on how every clip is trimmed, retimed, cropped, and nested, so knowledge about the footage holds only for particular uses of it, and an invalid edit can leave the timeline structurally broken. Existing video editing agents keep their edits valid with critic agents, reviewers, or restricted output formats. We present Cassette-Editor, a video editing agent with a deliberately simple interface: one tool reads the project and one tool writes to it. Every write passes through the same executor, rules, and commit service as the user's manual edits, and either commits atomically or is rejected with located diagnostics and repair options, while the model keeps the creative choices and decides how to recover. Reads relate stored analysis of the footage to each use of it on the timeline. In a controlled experiment, a real model is shown 277 of its own committed edits after damaging them. It corrected nearly every call with full or minimal feedback, but locating each problem cut the input tokens a correction needed to less than half, and its corrections dropped other values the model had written in one case rather than seven.

☆ Temporal Dynamics and Security Assessment of SRT Protocol: A 96-Day Longitudinal Analysis of Production Streaming Infrastructure
Ahmed F. K. Koysha, Ferdi Sönmez
This study presents a 96-day longitudinal analysis of Secure Reliable Transport (SRT) protocol behavior in a production streaming environment between Iraq and Turkey, examining 262,672 transport metric samples and 5,033,104 system resource measurements collected between October 2025 and January 2026. The research addresses temporal patterns, system-resource relationships, attack vulnerability, and anomaly detection. Results reveal significant temporal variation: Negative Acknowledgment exhibits 7.6-fold hourly variation and 11.5-fold daily variation (p < 0.001), though with small effect sizes (eta^2 < 0.04), indicating that temporal period explains less than 4 percent of total variance. Central Processing Unit (CPU) utilization emerges as the strongest system-level correlate of transport variation (r = 0.617 with NAK rate). Controlled User Datagram Protocol (UDP) flood experiments at 500 packets per second cause CPU increases of 176 to 806 percent, while SRT transport metrics change by only plus or minus 13 percent demonstrating protocol resilience through the Automatic Repeat Request mechanism. An unexpected anomaly reaching 97.7 percent CPU enabled signature-based differentiation between attack types. A Z-score anomaly detection method outperforms fixed thresholds, detecting all 7 security events. This study contributes the longest temporal characterization of SRT metrics reported to date, the first system-SRT correlation analysis, and the first controlled security assessment of SRT infrastructure. These findings provide actionable guidance for capacity planning, security hardening, and multi-metric monitoring of production SRT deployments.

☆ Applicability and Generalization of Audio Fingerprinting Methods to Speech SP
Kemal Altwlkany, Elmedin Selmanovic, Sead Delalić, Emanuel Lacic
Audio fingerprinting methods identify audio based on its content, even when the content has been possibly corrupted. Despite their applicability and usage in the speech domain, research and advancements in audio fingerprinting traditionally focus on music and are almost exclusively evaluated on music. We provide insights into speech-oriented audio fingerprinting by benchmarking the best performing audio fingerprinting models on speech data while taking into consideration the effects of noise, reverberation, temporal changes, pitch modifications, and lossy compression. Our findings indicate that audio fingerprinting methods based on self-supervised learning outperform classical approaches on speech data, while the performance of these models on speech is inferior compared to the performance that they achieve on music. Results also include an analysis of false positives, showing that fingerprinting methods are more likely to match with an audio of the same speaker rather than an audio of the same text, when mismatches occur.

☆ Multi-View Structural Representations for Physically-Consistent TeX Generation
Daoheng Li, Jianjun Qian*, Mengkai Yan, Jian Yang
Infrared and visible images provide complementary cues for low-light image generation, and physics-based methods can better exploit this complementarity. However, existing physics-based methods still rely heavily on paired data. To address these limitations, we propose Multi-View Routing Mixture-of-Experts (MVR-MoE), a framework for physically consistent TeX generation that learns multi-view structural representations. MVR-MoE mines intrinsic structural cues from infrared and visible images to organize them into multi-view representations, while the proposed multi-view hyper connections expand the feature space and preserve both shared evidence and modality-specific details. A hierarchical routing mechanism further regulates feature utilization at both the structural-view level and the expert level, enabling adaptive exploitation of heterogeneous cues. The predicted temperature, emissivity, and texture maps are constrained by the Stefan-Boltzmann law to ensure physically consistent. Extensive experiments on challenging datasets demonstrate that MVR-MoE achieves superior robustness and discriminability while remaining lightweight.

SenseNova, Joint Research Team, Zhongang Cai, Ziang Cao, Tailai Chen, Han Chong Chua, Linjun Dai, Hanming Deng, Hokin Deng, Haiwen Diao, Chenjing Ding, Weichen Fan, Xiao Fu, Zerui Gong, Chenyang Gu, Zexin He, Zhi Hou, Bo Li, Qinyue Li, Quanzhou Li, Xiaowan Li, Zhichao Liao, Dahua Lin, Zilong Lin, Bo Liu, Chunxiao Liu, Pengfei Liu, Tianqi Liu, Ziwei Liu, Chen Change Loy, Lewei Lu, Jiapeng Luo, Yuexiao Ma, Liang Pan, Xingang Pan, Oscar Qian, Ziyi Shang, Yuyao Shao, Dawei Su, Dacheng Tao, Qingyi Tao, Quan Wang, Ruisi Wang, Xiaogang Wang, Ziyi Wang, Beichen Wen, Donghao Wu, Jiaxu Wu, Silei Wu, Xiaoming Wu, Zhonghua Wu, Hongcan Xiao, Weiye Xu, Atsushi Yamashita, Lei Yang, Zhe Yang, Baiqiao Yin, Wanqi Yin, Hanfei Zhao, Tianbo Zhong, Long Zhuo, Jing Zuo

We conduct a large-scale evaluation across 12 representative benchmarks spanning tabletop manipulation, humanoids, mobile platforms, and dexterous hands. Under a unified protocol that allows in-context learning (ICL) from training-set demonstrations and substantially increases the number of execution steps, GPT-6-Astra achieves unprecedented performance (Fig. 1). Future research may focus on improving 1) the generality of ICL 2) cost and execution time, 3) physical-state verification, 4) recovery from irreversible failures, and 5) long-horizon preservation of progress. Second, we study the agentic harness for embodied control. We identify that close-loop coordination between a high-level "System 2" reasoner (i.e., GPT-6-Astra) and a low-level "System 1" controller (e.g., π0.5) is costly but effective. Third, we examine GPT-6-Astra on real-world deployment. Our experiments on 8 robot configurations reveal substantial gaps: 1) robot demonstrations required for ICL are expensive to collect, and 2) it is implausible to trade longer execution for higher success rates with physical constraints. Fourth, we envision the next generation of embodied benchmarks. ☆ Channel-Level Mask Guidance for Slimmable Image Compression
Chen Chen, Chenggang Wu, Yongbiao Chen, Weidong Qiu, Zhengwei Qi, Haibing Guan
Learned image compression (LIC) has achieved promising rate-distortion performance, but most methods lack scalability for diverse platforms with varying computational and storage constraints. Existing slimmable LIC methods achieve flexible complexity via consecutive-channel activation but suffer from two limitations: forced consecutive-channel selection degrades narrow-model performance at low bitrates, and the lack of stable variable-rate control limits adaptability to varying bandwidth. We propose a channel-level mask-guided slimmable image compression method. A learnable channel-wise mask with sparsity-promoting regularization enables non-contiguous top-w channel selection, letting narrow models use the most informative channels. After training, mask merging and channel reordering convert the model into a standard slimmable network via Mask-to-Slimmable (M2S) conversion, enabling efficient inference without architectural changes. For variable-rate control, we combine lambda- and width-conditioned modulation with quantization-step scaling and a progressive training pipeline stabilized by a freeze-then-fine-tune strategy. Experiments on Kodak across E2E, Hyperprior, and Checkerboard backbones show superior rate-distortion performance across widths and bitrates, with large gains for narrow models at low bitrates. At w=48, it achieves up to 19.22%, 24.11%, and 22.76% BD-rate savings over the same-width Slimmable baseline on E2E, Hyperprior, and CKBD, respectively. A single VBR model replaces 40 independent models, reducing storage by 14.8x to 15.9x. Code: https://github.com/sjtu-tcloud/MGSIC.

Data assimilation (DA) estimates the state of an evolving dynamical system from noisy, partial observations, and is widely used in scientific simulation as well as weather and climate science. In practice, filtering methods rely on frame-to-frame transition models. However, these models are fragile when observations are non-Markovian (when they form only a partial slice of a higher-dimensional latent state as in real-world weather data): they tend to accumulate errors over long horizons. At the same time, learned DA methods typically commit to a single regime, either filtering (nowcasting, real-time forecasting) or smoothing (retrospective reanalysis), which splits what should be a shared prior across application-specific pipelines. To address both issues, we introduce ForcingDAS, a unified and robust DA framework. Built on Diffusion Forcing with an independent noise level assigned to each frame, ForcingDAS learns a joint-trajectory prior instead of frame-to-frame transitions. This allows it to capture long-horizon temporal dependencies and reduce error accumulation. In addition, the same trained model spans the full filtering to smoothing spectrum at inference time. Specifically, nowcasting, fixed-lag smoothing, and batch reanalysis are selected through the inference schedule alone, without retraining. We evaluate ForcingDAS on 2D Navier-Stokes vorticity, precipitation nowcasting, and global atmospheric state estimation. Across all settings, a single model is competitive with or outperforms both learned and classical baselines that are specialized for individual regimes, with the largest gains observed on real-world weather benchmarks.

Phase one involves working with a publicly available dataset, while phase two focuses on training models on a private dataset within secure hospital networks. Accurate image registration is crucial in oncology, particularly for dynamic treatment adjustments in image-guided radiotherapy, where precise alignment is necessary to minimise radiation exposure to healthy tissues while effectively targeting tumours. This work details the methodology and data behind the OncoReg Challenge and provides a comprehensive analysis of the competition entries and results. Findings reveal that feature extraction plays a pivotal role in this registration task. A new method emerging from this challenge demonstrated its versatility, while established approaches continue to perform comparably to newer techniques. Both deep learning and classical approaches still play significant roles in image registration, with the combination of methods, particularly in feature extraction, proving most effective.

We propose MixiSpeech, a progressive state distillation framework that converts a multi-step conditional-flow acoustic model into a one-step generator while preserving its architecture and speaker conditioning. Rather than training the one-step model directly, MixiSpeech progressively reduces the global sampling budget through a 10-4-2-1 curriculum, with each student trained to match local teacher-integration endpoints using a masked state-matching objective. We instantiate the framework on a 710-speaker Vietnamese Matcha-TTS model trained from scratch on PhoAudiobook. On 100 shared test text-speaker pairs, direct one-step inference substantially degrades synthesis quality, obtaining 1.6846 UTMOS22-Strong and 6.21% WER compared with 2.2923 and 4.65% for the 10-step teacher. In contrast, the distilled one-step model achieves 2.2678 UTMOS22-Strong, 4.63% WER, and 2.83% CER, recovering most of the quality lost at the one-step operating point while requiring only a single acoustic vector-field evaluation. End-to-end inference time decreases from 0.0662 s for the 10-step teacher to 0.0312 s for MixiSpeech, corresponding to a 2.12 measured speedup. These results show that progressive state distillation can make one-step conditional-flow TTS practical without relying on a large multi-step sampling budget. TED queries audio-free windows with the transcript for Temporal Alignment and Forecasting, or answer candidates for Cross-Modal Temporal Binding, then aggregates evidence relative to that interval. Across four frozen AV-LLMs on SVHalluc, Temporal Forecasting accuracy rises from 29.3-33.7% under full-video questioning to 79.3-82.2% with TED. Query replacement reduces recovery; the observed anchor remains beneficial when temporal-region availability is held fixed. The findings distinguish locally recoverable evidence from successful full-video decisions, motivating explicit separation of narration content, utterance timing, and time-indexed visual evidence.

♻ ☆ Re:Cognize -- A Framework For Open-Set Comic Character Re-Identification NeurIPS
Aaditya Baranwal, Madhav Kataria, Yogesh S Rawat, Shruti Vyas
Comics and manga tell stories through characters whose appearances change from panel to panel, yet readers recognise them hundreds of pages later without ever consulting a cast list. Character re-identification models rarely face the same challenge: existing evaluations give them a fixed set of identities before the story begins. \textbf{Re:Cognize} instead asks models to recognise characters as the story unfolds and learn who is who along the way. Across three manga corpora, we evaluate five Re-ID backbones and \textbf{MECHA}, a memory-augmented baseline we introduce, and find that the central difficulty lies somewhere unexpected. Recognising familiar characters is nearly solved. Knowing which matches to trust is not. When models build a gallery and grow it from their own predictions, their performance deteriorates, even though correct identity labels would improve it by over twenty points. This raises a simple question: when should a model trust its own match? We derive a single comparison that determines when gallery updates improve recognition and use it to design \textbf{VOUCH}, which updates its memory only when the page provides supporting evidence. Without fitting additional parameters, VOUCH recovers between one-third and two-thirds of the improvement available from perfect labels. RE:COGNIZE measures whether a model can recognise characters as it reads; VOUCH shows how to remember them reliably. We focus our methodological claims on identity maintenance for previously encountered characters, while separately evaluating new-character emergence as a diagnostic under a fixed reference rule to distinguish recognition from discovery.

Across five 2D backbones and three 3D benchmarks, SGAV-MP preserves FP32-level Dice and high uncertainty-map agreement, achieving $3.59\times$--$7.8\times$ compression in 2D and $4.73\times$--$7.82\times$ in 3D. We find that a component shared by all fingerprints of the same model inflates the standard signed peak-to-correlation energy (sPCE). To counter this, we propose $Δ$sPCE: the sPCE between a query image and a candidate camera's fingerprint, minus the mean sPCE between that image and the fingerprints of the remaining candidates, in the spirit of T-norm score normalization. $Δ$sPCE improves attribution accuracy, suggesting that the device-specific PRNU signal is still present. In today's world-where social networks play a significant role-images serve as one of the most important tools for transferring concepts. In this work, a model for impulse noise image restoring is proposed by using a Minimax Concave Penalty. The proposed model is applicable to both color and grayscale images. Then, a numerical algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers is introduced, and the convergence of the method is analyzed both theoretically and numerically. In the final step, the proposed method is evaluated through simulations on several examples, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness.

Poisson equations frequently appear in various fields, such as mathematics, physics and informatics. Solving Poisson equation, however, is challenging. Traditional methods are not data-specific, although have high certainty. They require a large number of iterations due to the CFL numerical stability. In contrast, deep learning methods are data-driven and more efficient, but require accurate training data and suffer from heavy computation. To tackle these issues, we propose a wavelet-inspired Poisson solver with 24 trainable scalars. The proposed network has several advantages. First, it is compact. It has four independent $5\times5$ kernels, each represented by six parameters, leading to 24 scalars in total. Such compact format can be deployed on most devices. Second, thanks to the loop design, it achieves higher accuracy than previous methods. A residual loop reuses the wavelet block without increasing its parameters. Numerical experiments confirm that such loop indeed improves the solving accuracy. On 10000 images, one, two, and three loops of the wavelet block lead to PSNRs of $47.27$, $74.14$, and $100.74$ dB, respectively. Third, the proposed method is computationally fast. Thanks to the wavelet transform, the proposed method has linear computation complexity, leading to high computation performance. In short, we propose a novel looped wavelet neural network with compactness, accuracy and efficiency for solving Poisson equations. Our method can be applied in various fields, such as computational fluid dynamics, image reconstruction, biomedical engineering, electromagnetic field simulation.

♻ ☆ Authenticated Contradictions from Desynchronized Provenance and Watermarking CVPR 2026
Alexander Nemecek, Hengzhi He, Guang Cheng, Erman Ayday
Cryptographic provenance standards such as C2PA and invisible watermarking are positioned as complementary defenses for content authentication, yet the two verification layers are technically independent: neither conditions on the output of the other. This work formalizes and empirically demonstrates the $\textit{Integrity Clash}$, a condition in which a digital asset carries a cryptographically valid C2PA manifest asserting human authorship while its pixels simultaneously carry a watermark identifying it as AI-generated, with both signals passing their respective verification checks in isolation. We construct metadata washing workflows that produce these authenticated fakes through standard editing pipelines, requiring no cryptographic compromise, only the semantic omission of a single assertion field permitted by the current C2PA specification. To close this gap, we propose a cross-layer audit protocol that jointly evaluates provenance metadata and watermark detection status, achieving 100% classification accuracy across 3,500 test images spanning four conflict-matrix states and three realistic perturbation conditions. Our results demonstrate that the gap between these verification layers is unnecessary and technically straightforward to close.

We propose NESA, a Non-stationary Evidence-aware Semantic Alignment framework that replaces static prototype matching with an evolving alignment trajectory. To preserve semantic correspondence under evidence removal, it constructs adaptive alignment states from text-derived clinical semantics, full-view ECG context, and residual ECG evidence. This trajectory guides the ECG encoder to capture complementary diagnostic cues rather than rely on a small set of tokens. Experiments with MIMIC-IV-ECG pretraining and three downstream benchmarks show improvements in zero-shot diagnosis and label-efficient transfer. Dominant-token deletion analysis further indicates that NESA preserves cross-modal alignment after highly aligned ECG evidence is removed, supporting more distributed ECG-text grounding.

☆ Evidence Field: Adaptive Covering Programs for Medical Imaging
Isarar Siddique, Raiyan Siddique, Arshi Niyaz, Jamyang Ugyen Tshomo, Atish Raza
Medical image classifiers typically return predictions without a native contract for independently reconstructing their spatial decision computation. Evidence Field is a trainable spatial-program architecture that jointly produces class scores, selected covering programs and signed evidence. Its encoder combines absolute and image-relative response fields with associative spatial moments and learned characteristic sums. A typed classifier scores individual regions and parent-conditioned multiplicative groups; a covering recursion selects scale, partition and composition. We establish exact one-fold coverage, optimality within the registered grammar, a bound relating smooth training to hard inference, signed-score conservation and class-centred offset invariance. Direct contractions and their adjoint specify arithmetic and storage scaling on two- and three-dimensional grids. Native output records bind inputs, parameters, supports, types and contextual dependencies to individual and ensemble predictions. In a separately reported histopathology application, patient-separated training and evaluation across held-out centres provide empirical evidence for the architecture. Trained mechanism and corrected-loss comparisons distinguish predictive effects from implementation correctness; independent readers reconstruct descriptors, routes, scores and probability mixtures. The principal contribution is a coupled representation, decision and evidence architecture whose selected computation can be reproduced independently.

☆ Severity-Channel Conditioning: An Injection-Level Study for Consumer-Device Deblurring

Motion-deblurring models lose substantial accuracy when transferred from professional cameras to smartphone-derived imagery. This paper studies whether a severity descriptor, partly derived from the paired sharp target, helps adaptation on the iPhoneBlur consumer-device benchmark. Under a shared update budget, input concatenation of a severity map is compared with global feature modulation by capture metadata, spatial feature modulation by the severity map, and a tier-contrastive output objective, together with an unconditioned spectral-loss control, all fine-tuned from the same domain-adapted latent-diffusion baseline. The primary experiment is an oracle diagnostic: target-derived information is supplied at inference. For the evaluated model pair, input concatenation improves overall peak signal-to-noise ratio from 31.23 to 31.30 dB, whereas feature modulation, the contrastive objective, and the spectral-loss control do not exceed the baseline. The gain is positive on 87.2% of test images and on 14 of 15 held-out source videos; this video-level analysis describes the evaluated checkpoint pair and does not establish robustness to retraining, and three training seeds are reported separately. The input-level gain recurs on a transformer backbone. In one exploratory run, zeroing the channel at inference retains most of the gain in peak signal-to-noise ratio but lowers structural similarity below the baseline. A normalized-step diagnostic does not support the expected larger-gradient explanation. The results characterize the evaluated configurations and do not establish injection location as the sole cause, a spatial-locality mechanism, or a reliable deployment advantage.

☆ Codec-Compatible Learned Compression for 3D Gaussian Splatting
Feiyang Yu, Qi Yang, Wenjie Huang, Yunfeng Guan, Yiling Xu, Zhu Li
Video-based 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) compression methods provide a practical route by representing Gaussian attributes as 2D maps and coding them with standard video codecs. Among these maps, high-dimensional non-DC spherical harmonics (SH-AC) maps contain the largest number of channels and account for a dominant portion of the bitstream. However, their statistics differ substantially from those of natural images, and the nonlinear dependencies among SH-AC coefficients remain insufficiently exploited. To address these issues, we propose CCT-GS, a Codec-Compatible learned Transform framework for 3DGS compression. CCT-GS first learns a generalized SH-AC transform that captures cross-scene regularities and converts SH-AC maps into compact codec-friendly bottleneck maps. It further introduces LoRA-based scene adaptation to recover scene-specific appearance details with lightweight side information. Experiments on MPEG GSC sequences demonstrate that CCT-GS consistently outperforms representative video-based baselines, achieving an average BD-rate reduction of 51.30% over the video-based anchor.

♻ ☆ RePrior: Measurement-Reconciled Prior Correction for Sparse-View CBCT Reconstruction
Mengrui Yin, Tianxingjian Ding, Wufan Zhao, Ziyang Yan, Yu Tian
Sparse-view cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is severely under-constrained by limited X-ray projections. Learned reconstruction can provide complementary anatomical information, but using it as a prior in patient-specific Gaussian reconstruction introduces two challenges. First, the discrepancy between the learned prior and current reconstruction is spatially non-uniform: some local differences contain useful missing 3D information, whereas others reflect prior bias. Second, even a volumetrically beneficial correction can conflict with the observed X-ray measurements. Since X-ray measurements are line integrals, spatially separated corrections may affect overlapping rays, with their signed projection responses reinforcing or partially canceling in the measurement residual, so their feasibility cannot always be assessed independently. In this paper, we introduce RePrior, a multi-stage progressive prior-correction framework that addresses correction actionability, measurement feasibility, and representation expressivity. Selective Correction Proposal (SCP) first identifies actionable signed local corrections from prior--reconstruction discrepancies. Measurement-Constrained Reconciliation (MCR) then jointly enforces their consistency with patient-specific X-ray measurements, while Hybrid Residual Enhancement (HRE) recovers additional correction capacity through complementary voxel- and Gaussian-domain degrees of freedom around the reconciled anchor. RePrior requires neither test-time ground truth nor case-specific network fine-tuning. RePrior gains approximately 2.6~dB in 3D PSNR over R$^2$-Gaussian across LUNA16, PANORAMA, and PENGWIN. Beyond prior-assisted reconstruction, it delivers additional gains in volumetric quality and observed-view projection fidelity, with consistent gains in held-out-view fidelity in the backbone-matched evaluation.
♻ ☆ Authenticated Contradictions from Desynchronized Provenance and Watermarking CVPR 2026
Alexander Nemecek, Hengzhi He, Guang Cheng, Erman Ayday
Cryptographic provenance standards such as C2PA and invisible watermarking are positioned as complementary defenses for content authentication, yet the two verification layers are technically independent: neither conditions on the output of the other. This work formalizes and empirically demonstrates the $\textit{Integrity Clash}$, a condition in which a digital asset carries a cryptographically valid C2PA manifest asserting human authorship while its pixels simultaneously carry a watermark identifying it as AI-generated, with both signals passing their respective verification checks in isolation. We construct metadata washing workflows that produce these authenticated fakes through standard editing pipelines, requiring no cryptographic compromise, only the semantic omission of a single assertion field permitted by the current C2PA specification. To close this gap, we propose a cross-layer audit protocol that jointly evaluates provenance metadata and watermark detection status, achieving 100% classification accuracy across 3,500 test images spanning four conflict-matrix states and three realistic perturbation conditions. Our results demonstrate that the gap between these verification layers is unnecessary and technically straightforward to close.

♻ ☆ SLIM: Semantic-based Low-bitrate Image compression for Machines ACCV 2026
Hyeonjin Lee, Jun-Hyuk Kim, Jong-Seok Lee
In recent years, the demand of image compression models for machine vision has increased dramatically. However, the training frameworks of image compression still focus on the vision of human, preserving unnecessary details and limiting bitrate efficiency for machine vision tasks. In this paper, we propose Semantic-based Low-bitrate Image compression for Machines, termed SLIM. This proposed framework consists of two key components: RoI-focused latent compression and semantic latent enhancement with dual cues. First, the latent compressor is trained to focus on Region-of-Interest (RoI) areas that are semantically and functionally important for machine vision tasks in the latent space, while requiring no explicit masks during inference. Second, to compensate for severe information loss at extremely low bitrates, a diffusion-based semantic decoder enhances the compressed latent with a pretrained diffusion model guided by two complementary cues provided by an RoI-focused latent and text-based semantic guidance. This design preserves RoI details that are critical for machine perception while maintaining semantically coherent and artifact-suppressed non-RoI regions under extremely low bitrates. Experimental results show that SLIM consistently achieves strong performance across diverse machine vision tasks under the same bits per pixel condition, compared to conventional image compression models for machines. Our code is available at https://github.com/mcml-official/SLIM

♻ ☆ Solving Inverse Problems via Diffusion-Based Priors: An Approximation-Free Ensemble Sampling Approach
Haoxuan Chen, Yinuo Ren, Martin Renqiang Min, Lexing Ying, Zachary Izzo
Diffusion models (DMs) have proven to be effective in modeling high-dimensional distributions, leading to their widespread adoption for representing complex priors in Bayesian inverse problems (BIPs). However, current DM-based posterior sampling methods proposed for solving common BIPs rely on heuristic approximations to the generative process. To exploit the generative capability of DMs and avoid the usage of such approximations, we propose an ensemble-based algorithm that performs posterior sampling without the use of heuristic approximations. Our algorithm is motivated by existing work that combines DM-based methods with the sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) method. By examining how the prior evolves through the diffusion process encoded by the pre-trained score function, we derive a modified partial differential equation (PDE) governing the evolution of the corresponding posterior distribution. This PDE includes a modified diffusion term and a reweighting term, which can be simulated via stochastic weighted particle methods. Theoretically, we prove that the error between the true posterior and the empirical distribution of the generated samples can be bounded in terms of the training error of the pre-trained score function and the number of particles in the ensemble. Empirically, we validate our algorithm on several inverse problems in imaging to show that our method gives more accurate reconstructions compared to existing DM-based methods. Our code is available at the following Github repository~\url{https://github.com/HaoxuanSteveC00/AFDPS-TMLR}.

☆ Joint, Decoupled, or Agent: When Each Multimodal Alignment Paradigm Wins
Yi Fang, Gaurav Srivastava, Sirui Ding, Xuan Wang
Jointly pretrained multimodal encoders are a common way to combine modalities, while alternatives integrate their information during downstream training or inference. When does each approach win? We compare three paradigms, instantiated with public checkpoints, across 16 paired datasets in five domains and multiple training-label budgets. JOINT trains a fusion head on frozen, jointly pretrained encoders. DECOUPLED trains a fusion head on frozen, independently pretrained encoders. AGENT gives a frozen LLM task instructions, labelled examples, available sample text, and supervised unimodal readouts. No paradigm dominates the complete 144 dataset-budget combinations: DECOUPLED wins 54, JOINT 44, and AGENT 46 by mean utility. ScienceQA, MELD, and MetMeme shift from AGENT to fusion as supervision increases. Between the fusion paradigms, JOINT leads on four of five QA datasets across all evaluated budgets, while higher unimodal 5-NN accuracy is associated with a relative shift toward DECOUPLED across eight classification datasets (Spearman $ρ=-0.67$). We test whether representation and task diagnostics predict these preferences on held-out datasets before fitting their candidate systems. A two-step cascade combines these diagnostics with task and budget metadata to select AGENT or fusion, then JOINT or DECOUPLED. Under leave-one-group-out evaluation, it selects the winner in 71.4% of cells versus 54.2% for metadata-only routing, with mean relative regret 0.028 versus 0.057. Using geometry, supervised representation diagnostics, and text-label matching together yields higher accuracy and lower regret than using any one of these sources with metadata. These results connect paradigm preferences to supervision budget, task format, and unimodal 5-NN accuracy. Target-task diagnostics thus support selecting among the three paradigms before candidate fitting.
☆ Semantic-Critical Regions for Video-to-Audio Generation
Yun Fang, Wei Guo, Zhuonan Liang, Heng Wang, Weidong Cai
In real-world videos, sound events are often associated with localized and fine-grained visual cues, such as object motion, object-part dynamics, contact events, and interactions between objects. Existing video-to-audio (V2A) methods employ implicit conditioning based on global visual representations or explicit control derived from temporal and spatial cues. However, subtle sound-producing and sound-indicative interactions remain insufficiently captured, leaving room for more precise visual conditioning of sound-event semantics and temporal dynamics. Motivated by this observation, we refer to regions containing such sound-relevant visual evidence as Semantic-Critical Regions (SCRs) and introduce SCR-V2A, a V2A generation framework that explicitly localizes and encodes SCRs as fine-grained visual guidance for audio generation. Specifically, we first identify SCRs through sound-related visual localization. We then transform the localized regions into a control representation through adapter-based dual visual encoding, which jointly captures global visual context and fine-grained sound-relevant evidence. The representation is used to condition a downstream audio generation model. Experiments on both in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks demonstrate that SCR-V2A achieves strong performance in distribution matching and audio quality while remaining competitive in cross-modal alignment and requiring few trainable parameters. These results highlight the value of prioritizing fine-grained, sound-relevant visual regions for V2A generation.

♻ ☆ Learning to Reason About Implicit Multimodal Harm: From Diagnosis to Generalization
Anisha Saha, Varsha Suresh, Teodora Kamova, Sophia Wiedmann, Timothy Hospedales, Vera Demberg
A benign image paired with a benign caption can become harmful only in combination, making detection fundamentally a cross-modal reasoning problem. Existing multimodal harm benchmarks evaluate only classification accuracy, leaving unclear whether models identify the cross-modal mechanism that produces harm. We introduce MuPHI (Multimodal Pragmatic Harm Interpretation), a controlled diagnostic benchmark in which harm arises purely from image-text composition, with benign counterfactuals and annotated harm rationales. Using MuPHI, we systematically evaluate where compositional harm reasoning breaks in vision-language models (VLMs). MuPHI reveals that VLMs reliably ground each modality yet fail to bind the evidence into the harm mechanism and their predictions respond weakly to label-determining counterfactual interventions. Moreover, existing harm detection approaches trained on labels substantially improves in-domain (ID) detection but transfers poorly across harm distributions. We therefore propose Compositional Harm Interpretation Learning (CHIL), which rewards evidence identification in each modality, cross-modal binding and verdict consistency in the reasoning chain rather than just predicted label. CHIL improves 81% OOD transfer evaluations by an average of +2.5 macro-F1 and correct counterfactual flip rate by up to +3.8 and +5.4 % points, while also improving overall reasoning quality over label-only optimization. These results suggest that optimizing how a model reasons, not just what it concludes, offers a promising direction for multimodal safety systems that generalize beyond dataset-specific correlations.
♻ ☆ TV-AudioRemover: Joint Text-Visual Guided Sound Removal with Multi-Task Hard-Mixture Curriculum
Xinyue Guo, Jianxuan Yang, Daiguo Zhou, Jiagao Hu, Yuxuan Chen, Fei Wang, Jian Luan
Visual object removal can eliminate a target from video frames, yet its acoustic trace persists in the soundtrack, causing obvious audio-visual inconsistency. Existing video inpainting models operate solely on pixels, while audio editing models, especially for the sound removal task, are typically driven by text and therefore rely on limited single-modal control, which is less effective than multimodal guidance that provides stronger semantic grounding and temporal synchronization cues. In this paper, we present Text-Visual Guided Sound Removal (TV-AudioRemover), a target sound removal framework that leverages the visually edited video together with a natural-language instruction to suppress the sound associated with the removed visual object from the original audio mixture. To acquire high-quality training data, we devise a pipeline to construct a million-scale dataset of single-object audio-visual aligned samples, from which we synthesize mixture-target pairs customized for model training. To effectively leverage visual context and follow instruction intent, we augment the model architecture with task tokens, generalizable instruction modeling, and modality-specific global guidance. We further adopt multi-task training to strengthen task-role comprehension, and employ a hard-mixture curriculum that leverages semantically similar acoustic mixtures during fine-tuning to enhance fine-grained source discrimination. To support evaluation, we present AV-Remove-Bench, a comprehensive audio-visual object removal benchmark, along with dedicated objective metrics and an MLLM-based evaluation protocol. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on both subjective and objective metrics. Project page: https://yjx-research.github.io/TV-AudioRemover/.

☆ LUMINR: Intensity-conditioned Meta-learned INRs for Accelerated Medical Image Registration
Damian Rynczak, Marek Wodzinski
Implicit neural representations (INRs) have been applied to deformable image registration, where a lightweight network maps a spatial coordinate to a deformation vector. Because an INR encodes one specific signal in its parameters, a fresh network must be optimized for every image pair at test time, which is slow. Existing methods reduce this cost by meta-learning an initialization across a population of image pairs, and condition the weights of the INR globally, so the same conditioning applies at every coordinate while the deformation field it initializes varies across the domain. We propose LUMINR, a meta-learning framework that accelerates this per-pair fitting and in which the conditioning is local instead. LUMINR uses an INR that maps a coordinate, together with local intensity and gradient features, to a deformation vector, so the conditioning varies over the domain at the resolution of the field being modelled. Its objective is to find an initialization of the INR parameters from which the network can be fine-tuned to register any unseen pair in only a few optimization iterations. We evaluate LUMINR on 3D deformable registration of brain MRI from the OASIS dataset, where local conditioning and the meta-learned initialization prove complementary: early in fitting they reach a markedly higher accuracy than either does alone. Fine-tuned from that initialization, LUMINR matches the accuracy of the same conditioned INR fit from scratch in roughly a tenth of the gradient steps and a tenth of the wall-clock time, while the deformation fields stay smooth with negligible folding.

Moinak Bhattacharya, Annie Singh, Mohammad Chaudhry, Prateek Prasanna, Gagandeep Singh
Background: Incomplete multiparametric MR examinations limit glioma characterization and downstream AI tools. Generative models can synthesize missing MRI sequences, but anatomical structure and clinically relevant tumor features are challenging to preserve. Two radiologists independently evaluated the anatomical fidelity, pathological representation, and overall image quality of the synthesized images. Results: GliomaINK exhibited the highest PSNR across all six MRI translation directions in both evaluation cohorts. In the BraTS-AG test set, the PSNR reached $25.64\pm0.55$ dB for the T2W-to-T1C synthesis, compared with $13.78\pm0.32$ dB for Pix2Pix and $18.90\pm0.53$ dB for SPADE. For downstream tumor segmentation, the method showed strong performance across tumor subregions with Dice scores reaching $0.928\pm0.014$ for edema, and $0.885\pm0.040$ for enhancing tumor. For the IDH1 mutation-status prediction, GliomaINK achieved the highest AUROC score in four of the six sequence configurations, reaching $0.827\pm0.088$. Conclusion: Anatomy-guided conditional flow matching enables high-fidelity cross-sequence glioma MRI synthesis demonstrating potential for preservation of clinically relevant information in synthesized MRI and improving downstream tasks.
♻ ☆ Diagnostic Impact of Cine Clips for Thyroid Nodule Assessment on Ultrasound
Jichen Yang, Brian C. Allen, Kirti Magudia, Lisa M. Ho, Chad M. Miller, Maciej A. Mazurowski, Benjamin Wildman-Tobriner
Objective: Thyroid ultrasound is commonly performed using a combination of static images and cine clips (video recordings). However, the exact utility and impact of cine images remains unknown. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of cine imaging on accuracy and consistency of thyroid nodule assessment, using the American College of Radiology Thyroid Imaging, Reporting and Data System (ACR TI-RADS). Methods: 50 benign and 50 malignant thyroid nodules with cytopathology results, from 89 patients, were included. A reader study with 4 specialty-trained radiologists was then conducted over 3 rounds, assessing only static images in the first two rounds and both static and cine images in the third round. TI-RADS scores and the consequent management recommendations were then evaluated by comparing them to the malignancy status of the nodules. Results: Mean sensitivity for malignancy detection was 0.65 for static images and 0.67 with both static and cine images (p=0.41). Specificity was 0.20 for static images and 0.22 with both static and cine images (p=0.25). Management recommendations were similar with and without cine images. Intrareader agreement on feature assignments was slightly lower when cine images were added (0.83 vs 0.87, p<0.001), and TI-RADS point totals changed more between rounds with cine images. Conclusion: The inclusion of cine imaging for thyroid nodule assessment on ultrasound did not significantly change diagnostic performance in this reader study, although it changed some feature assignments. Current practice guidelines, which do not mandate cine imaging, may be sufficient for TI-RADS-based management recommendations.
